newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Wednesday on profit-taking despite overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,650 yuan ($2,852) per tonne, losing 140 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,750 and hit a low of 23,610.
May fell 200 yuan to 23,080, June 190 to 23,390, July 100 to 23,580, August 150 to 23,630 and October 130 to 23,620.
Combined volume rose to 41,670 tonnes from 41,480.
Copper opened slightly lower and fell steadily for most of the session.

With most speculative hot money flowing to the stock markets, producers are increasingly using the futures market as a means of selling their physical copper by delivering the metal to close out short positions, brokers said.
This is the basic reason for Shanghai copper contracts moving against the LME trend, they said.

"A lack of follow-up buying interest made major institutional buyers cautious about pushing up prices, but selling from copper producers increased, which pulled the contracts down today," one broker said.
"The recent crazy performance on the stock markets has attracted a lot of speculative money," said another broker.
The price of physical copper is around 23,300 yuan in the Shanghai area.
Traders said they expected copper to test the 23,500-yuan support level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mostly down. May was unchanged at 15,310 yuan per tonne, June fell 50 to 15,550 and July 100 to 15,780.
Combined volume fell to 1,970 tonnes from 2,560.
